description: A credential the person holds that bears on crossing a border: a passport, a national identity card, a residence permit, a visa, an ETA or an EUDI PID. One type rather than several, because a residence permit is BOTH an identity document and an entitlement, and splitting identity from permission would force it to exist twice; `kind` says which it is and the `grants` block is present only when the document confers permission rather than merely attesting who you are. The field that makes this schema worth having is `field_provenance`. Where a value came from is not metadata here, it is the difference between an answer and a guess: an expiry read from the MRZ carries a check digit, a date of issue from DG12 is signed by the issuing state, and the same two values typed in by hand are a person's memory of a document they may not be holding. THE RULE THAT FOLLOWS, AND IT IS ABSOLUTE: a self-declared field may RAISE a question and may never CLOSE one. Nothing computed from an unattested value may be presented as a cleared requirement. `issuing_state` is kept separate from `nationality` because the MRZ carries both and they differ for refugee and stateless travel documents, where treating them as one silently produces the wrong rule. `document_code` is kept because it is what lets an agent refuse correctly — a diplomatic or service passport is not an ordinary one and must never be scored as though it were.

date_of_birth.description: Drives more than identity: minors need consent letters and birth certificates on a document checklist, and several fee schedules waive or reduce by age.

document_code.description: The MRZ document code — P for an ordinary passport, PD diplomatic, PS service, ID for a card. Kept so an agent can refuse correctly instead of assuming ordinary; a diplomatic page changes the applicable rule entirely.

expires_at.description: Date of expiry. The input to every "valid N months beyond departure" rule.

verification.description: `cryptographic` for a signed chip read or a verified credential, `checksum` for an MRZ line that passed its check digits, `none` for anything a person typed or a model read off a photograph.

field_provenance.description: Per FIELD, not per document: where that value came from and how strongly it is attested. A document is routinely part chip-read and part typed, and the two must never be weighed alike.

grants.description: Present only when this document confers permission — a visa, a permit, an ETA. A passport attests identity and grants nothing, and leaving this absent is how the difference is recorded.

class.description: The coded class, never free text — a Schengen C, a UK Skilled Worker, a US B1/B2. A residence permit's class is what a checklist keys on when a non-citizen resident must prove regular status.

in_document_ref.description: The `travel-document` this is affixed to — a visa sits in a passport, and replacing the passport does not void the visa.

issued_for_places.description: ISO alpha-3 codes this permission is good for. A Schengen visa lists many.

holder_ref.description: The `person` node this belongs to. Absent means the account holder.

issued_at.description: Date of issue. Lives in DG12 and NOT in the MRZ, which is why it is so often missing — and it is unanswerable-without for the ten-year condition that applies across most of the Schengen corpus.

issuing_state.description: ISO 3166 alpha-3 of the authority that issued it. Deliberately SEPARATE from `nationality`: the MRZ carries both and they differ for refugee and stateless travel documents. Collapsing them applies the wrong country's rule without any error being raised.

issuing_state_ref.description: Optional `place` node of kind country, when the code has been resolved.

label.description: What the person calls it — "my Indian passport", "the old one".

linked_refs.description: Every node id this record points at, flattened into one top-level array of bare UUID strings — the only shape the platform's traversal index can see. The typed refs below stay the source of truth; this is the index's view and must be rewritten whenever any of them changes.

nationality.description: ISO 3166 alpha-3 of the nationality the document attests.

number.description: The document number. SENSITIVE — this field is a candidate for `encrypted_fields` and should be turned on before any real document is stored. It is deliberately not a node reference, so encrypting it can never sever the graph.

photo_ids.description: rawfile nodes — a scan or photograph of the document.

resident_address_ref.description: A `place` node, structured rather than a city string. It decides the application route, which is a measured source of wrong answers: a resident of one country sent to another country's mission is a wasted appointment.

status.description: Retired by status, never deleted — a prior visa, including a refused one, is exactly the history a later checklist asks about.
